svg.text: Copper crossing: openable floor does not remove the thresholds
RWT-METALS / 30 October 2026 / all dimensions mm / conditional envelopes / no installed-safety result
A Located north crossing
Plan 1:35; axes and bands retained for comparison only
Garden threshold: 417.5
Each crossing still needs its own
supported, releasable pipe piece.
Family-room run: 3415
Dashed strip: old 650 opening
extended as a comparator only.
Cover/support, thermal continuity,
occupation and lifting unresolved.
Court threshold: 417.5
Both door apertures x4800–7200; pipe axes x5800/6200.
Joint-face positions, fixed W2 penetration and module lengths: unknown.
B Depth screen at two crossing-end slices
Envelope heights 1:8; horizontal positions diagrammatic
Near -270
Far -330
Near -380
Far -440
Red dashed depth: nominal 300 reserve, not a finished floor.
220 transverse flange; retained 60 fall. No support,
bolt/tool projection or release sweep has been included.
At equal stations: 400 centres + 220 = 620 wide;
old 650 gives 15 each outside edge before tools/supports.
Staggering or relocating joints changes the question.
C Renewal and retained water boundary
Old uninterrupted body 4450 / exterior reservation 5250.
Possible unopened bands 417.5 ≠ removable piece lengths.
220 intact flange still cannot pass a 160 bore.
W1 service-joint release must retain fixed W2 protection.
No actual W2 penetration, dry bay or shortened garden
handling area is proved by this diagram.
Development sequence
Divert rain; independently support; expose floor access;
release exact joints; show full module/threshold-piece sweep;
reinstate; test conveyed-water W1 and retained W2 separately.
See segmented-copper-access.md. Raised-terminal-section.md retains the separate ground/receiving-level comparison.
RWT-METALS remains planned. Materials, floor/support, actual removal, dry access and hydraulic acceptance remain open.
